name: KIT Campus North — KATRIN experiment and Tritium Laboratory
notes: No accelerator or beamline record exists for KIT in the atlas, so the KATRIN setup is represented by detector:katrin (outline) and the beamline is listed as unlocated against the facility.

The previous KIT worklog (GEOMETRY_desy-psi-kit.md) found no building for KATRIN because Overpass was down and Nominatim cannot search by tag. The element used here, way 394890935, was found through the OSM API bounding-box read.

summary.plain: KIT Campus North near Karlsruhe, drawn to scale with the footprint of the KATRIN neutrino-mass experiment and the two buildings of the Tritium Laboratory that supplies it. The experiment's roughly 70-metre beamline is not drawn as a line because no source gives its axis.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:kit-karlsruhe. OpenStreetMap: campus polygon (way 155843597, source=estimate), the KATRIN outline (way 394890935; 55.6 m long, bearing 16 degrees, 879 m2) typed experimental_area on detector:katrin, and TLK buildings 451 and 452 (ways 99082515, 99082477; 'Building 451/452' per the KIT TLK handout). The beamline (about 70 m, KATRIN paper arXiv:2103.04755) is unlocated: no sourced axis or end points.

unlocated.backlog: Find the as-built KATRIN site plan (the Technical Design Report update, or a KIT/KATRIN geodetic survey of the beam axis with coordinates of the WGTS and the detector end) and place the axis; or a KIT Campus North GIS layer with a stated licence that gives the spectrometer hall footprint. A line may be drawn only with a sourced azimuth and sourced end points, then checked against the 70 m figure.
unlocated.reason: KATRIN beamline axis and its component positions (windowless gaseous tritium source, transport section, pre-spectrometer, main spectrometer 23.23 m long, detector; overall length about 70 m). KATRIN states the orientation only as upstream south, downstream north, and no fetched source gives coordinates for the source, spectrometers or detector. The OSM outline drawn is 55.6 m long at a bearing near 16 degrees and shorter than the 70 m setup, so a beam line cannot be taken from it without inventing its end points.
